messages:
kelly: dropping a quick thread for the onboarding empty-state + first-run nudges. Want feedback on 1) banner vs inline helper 2) sample-project discovery 3) accessibility microcopy.

nina: love the idea of a contextual empty-state that surfaces 1 featured sample + a CTA. Banner feels heavy; inline helper (subtle card in the empty-state) is cleaner.

pat: agree inline. But make the CTA verb-first: "Run demo" not "Learn more". Also add a tiny hint: "Uses free credits" so users aren’t surprised.

omar: sample discovery: show featured demo + a secondary link "See more demos" that opens gallery. Keep gallery off the critical path.

a11y-bot: a11y checklist: empty-state card must have role=region and aria-label, CTA buttons need accessible names, and the hint badge must be text not just an icon. Ensure color contrast >= WCAG AA.

kelly: microcopy draft for empty-state: "Not sure where to start? Run a demo project to try Redwood with example data." Button: "Run demo". Small link: "See more demos". Inline privacy note: "Demos may send anonymous usage metrics." Thoughts?

privacy-bot: wording ok but change to "anonymous usage metrics (no request bodies stored)" for clarity. Also require explicit opt-in for EU users. No pre-checked boxes.

nina: UX idea: clicking "Run demo" opens a tiny confirmation popover (not full modal) that shows the selected demo, credit cost, and a checkbox "Enable anonymous usage metrics" (off by default). This is lightweight and explicit.

pat: prefer popover vs modal. Less disruptive. Popover should trap focus while open and have Esc to close. After run, show toast "Provisioning demo..." then "Demo ready". a11y-bot: ensure toast announcements are polite and not duplicated with route focus.

a11y-bot: yes. Plan: popover uses role=dialog; trap focus; checkbox has aria-describedby pointing to the long privacy line; toast uses aria-live=polite and we suppress it if we immediately move focus to new page heading.

kelly: good. Also mobile: the empty-state card becomes stacked with the CTA full-width. The popover should become a small sheet from bottom. Ensure it’s not full-screen unless confirm flow requires it.

omar: analytics: track `empty_state_shown`, `demo_popover_opened`, `demo_run_confirmed`, `telemetry_opt_in`. Let's correlate with time-to-first-request and onboarding completion.

dev-bot: implementation notes: server record consent (user_id, consent_boolean, method: onboarding_popover, timestamp). Events: `onboard.empty_shown`, `onboard.demo_clicked`, `telemetry.opt_in_onboard`. Use feature flag `onboard.empty_demo_v1`.

privacy-bot: also add a Settings -> Privacy toggle that reflects stored consent and lets users revoke. If revoked, ensure headers like `x-telemetry-opted-in` are removed from sample demo requests.

nina: design nit: where to put the 'Learn more' privacy link? Inline under the checkbox in the popover seems best.

pat: microcopy for popover (final suggestion): header: "Run demo project" body: "This demo provisions example resources and may send anonymous usage metrics (no request bodies stored)." [ ] Enable anonymous usage metrics (off by default) [Run demo] [Cancel] [What we collect]

a11y-bot: ensure `What we collect` opens content in a new tab and is keyboard reachable. Provide `aria-describedby` IDs for SRs.

kelly: decision summary: inline empty-state card with "Run demo" CTA -> opens confirmation popover with unchecked checkbox for telemetry + credits note -> one-time confirmation -> record consent server-side -> expose toggle in Settings. Feature flag rollout + analytics. Add a11y checklist to PR.

omar: I'll add the feature-flag and event tickets. kelly: please add the microcopy to the PR and ping legal for final review.

kelly: will do. Thanks — pushing updates to figma and opening PR now. End thread.
